findings.rationale: phUSD.mint (FlaxToken) reverts only on privileged authorization loss (setMinter(phlimboV3,false), revokeAllMintPrivileges() mintVersion bump, or canMint cleared). No unprivileged revert path, no supply cap, no pausability. revokeAllMintPrivileges() is phUSD's GLOBAL emergency kill-switch across the Phoenix ecosystem; a phUSD operator pulling it to contain an unrelated minter incident would be SURPRISED that it freezes every PhlimboV3 staker's principal (auto-claim mint reverts inside stake/withdraw/claim). Surprise => non-obvious footgun => in scope (Law 3). Recoverable (re-authorize minter) and privileged-only trigger => strictly less severe than M-05's unprivileged blocklist => Low, not Medium.
findings.severityJustification: Recoverable + privileged-only (owner/phUSD-governance) trigger. Only fires when desiredAPYBps>0 has produced pending phUSD AND minter authorization is subsequently lost. Materially lower likelihood than M-05's permissionless external blocklist. Report as Low operational hazard / incomplete-fix note. (Severity-classifier and severity-auditor to confirm; not to be escalated to Medium.)
findings.fixGuidance: Wrap the phUSD mint leg in a bank-on-failure path mirroring the stable/promo legs (mint-then-bank a phUSD IOU via try/catch preserving the principal path), OR operationally guarantee PhlimboV3's minter authorization is never globally revoked while V3 holds stake.

findings.title: PhlimboV3-side unclaimable stable/promo banked to MigratorV2V3 as beneficiary is unrecoverable: the migrator exposes no function that calls PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimableStable/Promo (owner emergencyTransfer only)
findings.category: stranded funds / missing recovery path (design gap)

relatedTo.V3-L-08 (faa2d9ba): NOT a duplicate. V3-L-08 is the migrator's OWN internal unclaimable bank (first-come reallocation on withdrawAll, no aggregate accounting). DEDUP-10-002 is the PhlimboV3-SIDE unclaimable*Of[migrator] bank that the migrator can never pull because it has no function calling PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimable*. Different bank, different contract-of-record, different fix.
relatedTo.V3-F-01 (3f241c3a): NOT a duplicate. F-01 is the migrate straggler-exclusion recovery-path faithfulness gap; this is a token-custody stranding on a failed reward leg.
relatedTo.V3-Q-01 (e1392170): NOT a duplicate. Q-01 is withdrawAll omitting promoToken sweep of the migrator's physical balance; this is PhlimboV3-side accounting credited to the migrator identity.

findings.rationale: banked stable -> unclaimableStableOf[MigratorV2V3] (:876) / promo -> unclaimablePromoOf[token][MigratorV2V3] (:902). Recovery requires msg.sender==MigratorV2V3 calling PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimableStable()/claimUnclaimablePromo(token). MigratorV2V3 has claimUnclaimable only for its OWN bank plus migrate/migrateOne/seedUsers/skipCurrent/withdrawAll -- none forwards into PhlimboV3's pulls. Stranded under the migrator identity; user not made whole (migrateOne balance-delta reads 0 on the failed leg). Owner emergencyTransfer can sweep the physical balance out-of-band, so no protocol loss.
findings.severityJustification: Exotic precondition: a USDC-class rewardToken (or partner promo token) blocklisting the migrator's OWN address during a straggler/second-pass migration where the user already holds a V3 position with accrued pending (first-pass stake early-returns at amount==0). Implausible in practice; owner-recoverable; no theft. Low/informational.
findings.fixGuidance: Force the auto-claim beneficiary to `user` on the migrator delegation path (banks accrue to a puller-capable EOA), OR add a thin pullV3Bank(token) forwarder on MigratorV2V3 that calls phlimboV3.claimUnclaimable* and re-forwards to user.
